clauses.reason: The only command in Executive Order 6557-C is its final operative paragraph, which reads: "Now, Therefore, I, Franklin D. Roosevelt, President of the United States, pursuant to the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, approved June 16, 1933, and otherwise, do hereby approve said Code of Fair Competition for the Raw Peanut Milling Industry.". The four numbered paragraphs before it are findings that the President made as the basis of the approval (application made, notice given, hearings held, the code complies with section 3(a)(1) and (2)); they command nothing and are not operative clauses. The approval states no period, condition, until-date or provisional approval. The approval was code-dependent: under section 3(b) of the Act the approved provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade or industry, under section 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations, and under section 3(f) a violation was a misdemeanor, so the approval operated only through section 3. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The resolution states no effective date other than its approval, so the approval ceased to operate on June 14, 1935. No held record shows this code cancelled or suspended before June 14, 1935. June 16, 1935 is not an end date: section 1 of the same resolution replaced the original two-year expiry of Title I with April 1, 1936, and nothing in the resolution defers section 2. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not as an end date.

inventory_overrides.reason: The machine inventory lists the four numbered findings as operative items, and its item 4 also sweeps in the closing "It appears" sentence and the approving paragraph. The findings (application, notice, hearings, compliance with section 3(a)) are recitals that command nothing; the only command is the final paragraph beginning "Now, Therefore" that approves the code. The corrected inventory is that one paragraph.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 6557-C (January 12, 1934) approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Raw Peanut Milling Industry under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. The held text is the American Presidency Project transcription (grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; Common Crawl capture 2025-09-16T02:39:27Z); the standing note applies: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved. The order recites four findings and then approves the code in one closing paragraph; the machine inventory is corrected to that paragraph. Because each command is dependent on the code and no held record shows an earlier end, the first end is the statutory repeal of the code approval and enforcement provisions by section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, effective June 14, 1935. Schechter, decided May 27, 1935, held the section 3 delegation unconstitutional; that is recorded as a validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not as an end date, because the judgment cancelled no approval. The antitrust-exemption proviso of the resolution is not settled by the held text for past action; whatever survives is an accrued effect, not continued operation of the approval.
